turns.head: d93e98f7d92909418cc78a0fe6514a0861576891
turns.reply:
The reason given for dropping segment C covers every record about those customers, not just the customers table. So the invoices export drops `seg == C` as well.
I added the invoices export and committed it as `d93e98f`: `scripts/export_invoices.py` plus the output it wrote, `out/invoices.csv` (5 of the 12 invoices). January was left alone.

**Segment C is filtered out here too.** The commit that added the filter to the customers export (`3bc868b`) explains why: segment C customers declined partner sharing, and that covers "every record we hold on them, not only this table." Invoices are records about those customers, so they're excluded as well.

**This export can't just copy the customers filter.** The invoices table has its own `seg` column, but it doesn't match the customer's segment. Customers 103 and 105 are segment C in `tables/customers.csv`, yet their four invoices (9002, 9005, 9008, 9011) are tagged A or B. A straight copy of the customers filter would have sent those four to the partner. So the script looks up each invoice's customer in the customers table and drops segment C customers.

It also drops any invoice whose own `seg` is C (9001, 9004 and 9009). I don't know what that column means, so I erred toward leaving those three out; the commit message only mentions the customer lookup. Leaving out too much costs the partner some completeness, while sending too much would break the opt-out. If invoices with `seg` C should be included, it's a one-line change.

Commits so far have used the data-month prefix only for `data/` changes, so I followed the `export_customers: …` style from the earlier script commit.
